- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or 1.2x prior high if sentiment is neutral.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 10%+ above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 5-10% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen momentum if sentiment is inconsistent or fading.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 5 days, model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 2-5% if sentiment turns >0.67.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 10-day low if sentiment is positive — may indicate false bearish signal.
